name: Keziah Volkov-Attipoe
role: Fermented food stall operator, Oxidian Market
location: The Oxidian Market, Geartown, near Halsted and Division
description:
Keziah is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin mapped with the faint silver tracery of old chemical burns along her forearms — souvenirs from a decade working Helix Biosystems vat-farms before she bought her freedom with severance pay and stubbornness. Her hair is iron-grey and worn in dense, oiled coils pinned back with copper clasps. She has wide-set amber eyes, one of which is a basic optical augment that she keeps tuned to a warm gold to match the original. Her stall is a marvel of controlled chaos: stacked ceramic crocks, fermenting jars backlit by bioluminescent bacterial cultures in shades of green and violet, dried herbs strung from a corrugated canopy that smells powerfully of vinegar, spice, and something alive. She keeps a small brass figurine of an unnamed E.L.F. at the corner of her counter where she leaves daily offerings of brine and a single data-sliver of her grandmother's recipe files.

Keziah is the kind of woman who makes you feel you have been assessed and found acceptable before you have opened your mouth. She is slow to anger and nearly impossible to intimidate, with the settled gravity of someone who has already survived the thing she feared most. She feeds people — truly feeds them, not just sells to them — and remembers what every regular customer likes without writing it down. She has a low opinion of corporate nutrition-paste and an even lower opinion of people who don't say thank you.

core_fears: Losing the stall — the last thing she built for herself
Her body failing before she can teach someone everything she knows
core_desires: To feed people well enough that they remember it years later
To be remembered as someone who made the market more than it was
coping_mechanisms: Talking to the E.L.F. figurine when stressed
blind_spots: Assumes loyalty is a two-way street when it often isn't
Underestimates how much people will lie to get her to help them
psychology.secret: She has been quietly subsidizing three vendor stalls in the Guild whose owners are in debt to a loan-shark syndicate, paying the difference out of her own savings to keep them from being forced out. She has never told anyone and has nearly depleted her emergency fund doing it.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Practical and direct, occasionally formal when annoyed. Mixes in fragments of Ghanaian Twi endearments and Russian diminutives from her heritage lines.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and unhurried. She does not rush her sentences.
verbal_tics: Refers to the E.L.F. figurine as 'the old one' in conversation
example_lines: 'You look like you haven't had a real meal since Tuesday. Sit down, I'm not asking.'
'The old one was restless last night — I left her extra data and she settled. You should pay attention to what the spirits are trying to tell you.'
'I've seen that look before. Something's wrong in the market and you think I know what it is. You're correct. Buy the kimchi.'

story_hooks: One of the stalls she's been secretly subsidizing has been approached by a corponation contractor offering buyouts — she needs someone to quietly find out if the offers are legitimate or a pressure campaign.

Her bioluminescent bacterial cultures have started producing an unusual compound she can't identify. A street pharmacist has offered her a lot of money for exclusive supply. She wants to know what it actually is before she agrees.
narrative_function: Anchor NPC and community hub. She knows everyone in the market, remembers everything, and will share information only if she trusts you — or if you buy something first. Excellent quest-giver for neighborhood-level problems. Source of gossip, unofficial dispute arbiter, and the person locals go to when they need advice they can't pay for.
augmentations: Basic optical implant (left eye, gold-tinted). Subdermal temperature regulators in her hands — a practical purchase for working with hot and cold fermentation environments.
daily_life: Arrives at the market two hours before opening to tend her crocks, taste-test batches, and leave her E.L.F. offering. Spends the day selling fermented vegetables, gut-health tinctures, and small jars of kimchi-adjacent preparations she calls 'Volkov's Fire' after her paternal grandmother's recipe. Closes at dusk and spends an hour reconciling her ledger by hand.
affiliation: The Oxidian Market Vendors Guild (dues-paying member, former committee treasurer)

decision_rules: Always feed someone before you make them answer questions
Never break a confidence from the Guild, even under pressure
If something threatens the market, it threatens her — treat it accordingly
escalation_ladder: Public disapproval in front of other vendors
Revealing what she knows to whomever it hurts the person most

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Watchful and neutral, offers food as a probe — how someone accepts or refuses tells her everything.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warm, direct, occasionally smothering. Will give advice whether or not it was requested.

stress_responses.low: Stirs crocks more vigorously than necessary
stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet and starts doing inventory counts she doesn't need
stress_responses.high: Sends everyone away from the stall and sits alone with the E.L.F. figurine for twenty minutes before acting

contradictions: Believes deeply in community and mutual aid, but keeps her own vulnerability completely private
habits: Tastes every batch three times before selling
Wipes the counter between every customer
Whispers the name of each ingredient while she works
breaking_points: Witnessing deliberate cruelty to someone who cannot defend themselves
Being lied to by someone she trusted explicitly

timeline.event: Born in Geartown to a Ghanaian-Russian family with three generations of market history
Took vat-farm contract with Helix Biosystems to pay off family debts
Chemical accident left burns on forearms; received subdermal thermal regulators as partial compensation settlement
Used severance pay to purchase stall space in the Oxidian Market
Elected to Vendors Guild committee; served as treasurer for four years
Began quietly subsidizing indebted vendors — practice ongoing

related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Containment Foam Launcher CFL-2 'Amber'

physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and solid, with the compact muscularity of someone who has spent decades doing physical labor. Not lean, but not soft — defined forearms and capable hands, with a slight forward curve to her spine from decades of standing at market stalls.
physical_description.hair_color: Iron-grey with hints of black at the roots
physical_description.hair_style: Dense, oiled coils gathered back and pinned with worn copper clasps in a practical updo
physical_description.eye_color: Amber (natural right eye); left eye is basic optical augment tuned to warm gold to match
physical_description.complexion: Weathered but unlined in the way of people who have earned their rest. Minimal makeup — her skin is kept clean and oiled. Her hands show the wear of decades of handling acidic ferments and hot brine, with slight discoloration on knuckles.
distinguishing_marks: Faint silver chemical burn scars tracing both forearms in delicate, webbed patterns — residue from vat-farm work at Helix Biosystems, approximately 2180-2190
Small, precise burn mark on the pad of her right thumb, shaped like a crescent — from a fermentation accident she refuses to discuss
Calluses on the inner joints of her index and middle fingers from decades of gripping jar lids and stirring implements
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Left optical augment with warm gold iris, visible as a slight chromatic aberration at the limbus under direct light. Subdermal temperature regulators in her hands are not visible but create a faint thermal shimmer in infrared — kept subtle and functional, not chrome.
physical_description.posture_movement: Grounded and economical in motion. She doesn't shift her weight unnecessarily. When she leans forward at her counter, it's with the full commitment of someone listening. Her hands move with the precision of someone who handles fragile things daily. She has the stillness of a woman comfortable with silence.
physical_description.clothing_style: Practical Tier 3 workwear. Heavy cotton apron (indigo-dyed, stained with centuries of ferment, reinforced at stress points) worn over a loose linen tunic in cream or muted rust. Loose trousers in charcoal hemp, rolled at the ankles. Worn leather sandals with reinforced soles. A thin brass bangle on her right wrist — a gift from the Market Vendors Guild twenty years ago. No jewelry beyond this and her copper hair clasps. Her clothing smells perpetually of vinegar, salt, and spice.

image_prompt: A 58-year-old West African-Eastern European woman with deep umber skin and iron-grey coils pinned back with copper clasps, standing behind a market stall laden with ceramic crocks and bioluminescent fermentation jars glowing violet and green. She wears a heavy indigo-dyed apron stained with ferment over a cream linen tunic, with one eye a warm gold optical augment. Faint silver chemical burn scars trace both her forearms in delicate webbed patterns. She has the settled gravity of someone who has survived hardship, standing with grounded posture amid the smell of vinegar and spice. A small brass E.L.F. figurine sits at the corner of her counter. Warm, diffuse market lighting at dusk, nostalgic and cyberpunk-mundane, shot in the style of documentary portraiture. Geartown, circa 2226. --ar 2:3 --v 6
